details.label: Summary
details.text: The risk of locally damaging wind gusts and hail may spread east of Severe Thunderstorm Watch 616 this evening, though a downstream watch is not expected

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Along an eastward-moving cold front, two clusters of loosely organized thunderstorms in Middle TN and eastern KY are tracking east-southeastward toward the eastern edge of Severe Thunderstorm Watch 616 this evening. Around 30-40 kt of midlevel west-northwesterly flow (per JKL/OHX VWPs) oriented perpendicular to the front will aid in the maintenance of these storms for the next hour or so -- before reaching the higher terrain. This will especially be the case into eastern TN -- where lower/middle 80s temperatures and upper 60s dewpoints remain in place. As a result, the risk of locally damaging wind gusts and hail may spread east of the watch. However, given the localized nature of the ongoing severe risk, a downstream watch is not expected

details.label: Summary
details.text: Several clusters of strong to severe storms continue over portions of WW615. Damaging winds remain possible with these storms. Some risk may continue into parts of northwestern AL this evening

details.label: Discussion
details.text: As of 2330 UTC, regional radar showed several clusters of strong to severe storms ongoing across portions of WW615. The most intense of these clusters, located near the MS/TN border has produced recent measured severe gusts. This should continue across portions of southern TN and northern MS where moderate to large buoyancy and 25-35 kt of deep-layer shear are present and supporting more organized multicell clusters. High PWATS (2+ inches) and clustering will promote stronger downdrafts capable of damaging/isolated severe gusts. The primary severe risk appears most likely along the southwestern flank of the leading cluster across north-central MS where stronger low-level convergence along the existing outflow may preferentially support maintenance of the ongoing storms/new development this evening. However, some severe risk is possible east of WW615 into parts of northwestern AL this evening. However, the environment farther east is cooler and somewhat drier with less overall buoyancy. Weaker vertical shear with southward extent also casts some uncertainty on longevity. Regardless, enough buoyancy and steep low-level lapse rates likely exist to support an isolated damaging wind threat

details.label: Summary
details.text: The risk of locally damaging wind gusts continues in the near term, though the severe risk should gradually decrease into central Pennsylvania. Therefore, a downstream watch should not be needed

details.label: Discussion
details.text: A strongly forced, north/south-oriented band of storms is tracking eastward across western PA, with additional pre-frontal cells evolving in the cooler air downstream. Given a well-established cold pool and around 30 kt of 0-6 km shear (per CCX VWP) oriented perpendicular to the gust front, the risk of locally damaging wind gusts will continue in the near term. However, the immediate downstream air mass is characterized by cooler surface temperatures/weaker buoyancy, which should tend to limit the severe risk with eastward extent into central PA this evening. Therefore, while a localized risk of strong/locally damaging wind gusts could persist slightly east of Severe Thunderstorm Watch 614, a downstream watch is not currently expected

details.label: Summary
details.text: Isolated damaging gusts and perhaps some hail are possible with scattered thunderstorms across WA, northern ID and into western MT. While an isolated severe storm is possible, a WW is unlikely

details.label: Discussion
details.text: As of 22 UTC, GOES WV imagery showed an arc of convection ongoing from the Columbia Basin to the northern Rockies associated with an upper low off the WA/OR coast. Diurnal heating of a modified/remnant monsoon air mass has resulted in weak buoyancy over much of the Northwest. Scattered thunderstorms have developed across the higher terrain and a weak wind shift across the western Columbia Basin. Storm coverage is forecast to increase over the next couple of hours through peak heating, coinciding with some intensification of the ongoing/anticipated storms. A belt of stronger southwesterly flow aloft is overspreading the weakly unstable air mass, supporting elongated mid and upper-level hodographs. This could result in some modest storm organization into clusters or transient supercells. Steep low and mid-level lapse rates, especially closer to the upper low over WA where mid-level temperatures are cooler, could support a few stronger updrafts capable of marginally severe hail and damaging downburst winds. While an isolated severe risk is possible from WA into northern ID and northwest MT, the weak buoyancy and limited moisture should limit overall storm organization/intensity such that a WW is unlikely

details.label: Summary
details.text: Storms are expected to increase in coverage while spreading eastward into this evening. The primary concern is locally damaging wind gusts. While a watch is not currently expected, trends are being monitored

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Thunderstorms are increasing in coverage along the Blue Ridge in western VA, potentially aided by increasing midlevel height falls preceding a broad midlevel trough approaching the region from the west. Over the next few hours, these storms should continue spreading eastward across western/central VA and northern NC. A warm, moist, and uncapped air mass downstream should support a modest increase in thunderstorm coverage. While midlevel lapse rates are limiting overall buoyancy (around 1000-1500 J/kg MLCAPE), an elongated midlevel hodograph (40 kt of 0-6 km shear per FCX VWP) could promote a few loosely organized clusters capable of producing locally damaging wind gusts. While the overall risk may remain too localized/sparse for a watch, trends are being monitored
